title: Weather App Speaks First: Samsung One UI 9.5 Delivers Alerts Before You Head Out

content_html:
Mobile weather apps have always been “ask and answer” tools—you open them only when you want to check, and otherwise they sit quietly in a folder. Samsung is now looking to change that passive approach. According to SamMobile on November 19, in the first beta of One UI 9.5, the Weather app is preparing an AI upgrade: before you set off for another city, it will proactively remind you to check the weather at your destination.

Trip clues are hidden in calendars and flights

The key to this upgrade is teaching the Weather app to “read your schedule.” When the system detects that a user plans to travel to another city, the app will show a “Check the weather before you leave” prompt. Tap “Try it,” and it will jump straight to the destination forecast. The trigger clues come from multiple sources: appointments or meetings you have scheduled in another city, or a cross-city flight the phone detects is about to depart, can all serve as the basis for the reminder.

Behind it is a PAC brain

Powering this feature is Samsung’s in-development Personal Agent Core (PAC) system. It can gather contextual information from One UI and multiple Google apps, piece together what the user is doing and where they are going next, and then use that to deliver a personalized experience. In other words, “check the weather before you leave” is just one appearance of this system—the real goal is to have the phone proactively connect the itinerary clues scattered across different apps and deliver the right information at the right time. A release date for the official version of One UI 9.5 has not yet been set. With the beta version scouting ahead, how far this proactive experience can ultimately go will depend on feedback from subsequent testing.
